Create boxplot of assay, rowData or colData.

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/plotBoxplot.R
plotBoxplot.Rd

This methods visualizes abundances or variables from rowData or colData.

plotBoxplot(object, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SummarizedExperiment'
plotBoxplot(
  object,
  assay.type = NULL,
  row.var = NULL,
  col.var = NULL,
  x = NULL,
  features = NULL,
  group.by = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

a SummarizedExperiment object.

...

Additional parameters for plotting. They are grouped below by the part of the plot they customise. Each layer has its own prefixed arguments (box.*, point.*, line.*, outlier.*). Arguments not listed here are passed on to ggpubr::stat_pvalue_manual() when p-values are shown (see "Significance" below). Anything else, such as titles, scales and themes, can be changed by adding ggplot2 layers to the returned plot, e.g. + labs(y = "Shannon").

Mapping variables to aesthetics

  • colour.by: NULL or character scalar. Specifies a variable from colData(x) or rowData(x) which is used to colour observations. (Default: NULL)

  • fill.by: NULL or character scalar. Specifies a variable from colData(x) or rowData(x) which is used to fill boxes and points. (Default: NULL)

  • size.by: NULL or character scalar. Specifies a variable from colData(x) or rowData(x) which is used to scale observation points. (Default: NULL)

  • shape.by: NULL or character scalar. Specifies a variable from colData(x) or rowData(x) which is used to shape observation points. (Default: NULL)

  • facet.by: NULL or character scalar. Specifies a variable from colData(x) or rowData(x) which is used to facet or group observations. Use "rownames" to draw each of features in its own facet. (Default: NULL)

  • pair.by: NULL or character scalar. Specifies a variable from colData(x) which is used to pair observation points. Paired points are joined with lines. (Default: NULL)

  • add.change: Logical scalar. Whether to colour paired observations by the change between time points. (Default: FALSE)

Layers

  • add.box: Logical scalar. Whether to add a boxplot layer. (Default: TRUE)

  • add.points: Logical scalar. Whether to add a point layer. (Default: TRUE)

  • add.proportion: Logical scalar. Whether to add a barplot layer denoting the proportion of observations above threshold. (Default: FALSE)

  • add.threshold: Logical scalar. Whether to add threshold as a horizontal line. The line is always added with add.proportion = TRUE. (Default: FALSE)

  • add.significance: Logical scalar. Whether to test and show the significance of differences between groups (see "Significance" below). (Default: FALSE)

Box layer

  • box.alpha: Numeric scalar. Transparency of the boxes. (Default: 0.5)

  • box.width: Numeric scalar. Width of boxes. (Default: 0.75)

  • outlier.size, outlier.colour, outlier.alpha, outlier.shape: Size, colour, transparency and shape of the outlier points of the boxplot layer, passed to geom_boxplot. Outliers are drawn only when add.points = FALSE; otherwise all observations are already shown as points. If NULL, ggplot2 defaults are used, and the shape defaults to point.shape. (Default: NULL)

Point layer

  • point.alpha: Numeric scalar. Transparency of points. (Default: 0.65)

  • point.shape: Numeric scalar. Shape of points. (Default: 21)

  • point.size: Numeric scalar. Size of points. (Default: 2)

  • point.colour: Character scalar. Colour of points. (Default: "grey70")

  • point.offset: Character scalar. Method for offsetting points so that they do not overlap. The available options include: "center", "compactswarm", "hex", "square", "swarm" (see beeswarm::beeswarm() for details), "frowney", "maxout", "minout", "pseudorandom", "quasirandom", "smiley", "tukey", "tukeyDense" (see vipor::offsetSingleGroup() for details), "jitter", and "none". If "none", offsetting is not applied. (Default: "jitter")

  • jitter.width: Numeric scalar. Width of jitter. (Default: 0.3)

  • jitter.height: Numeric scalar. Height of jitter. (Default: 0)

  • beeswarm.corral: Character scalar. Beeswarm's "corral" method. Fed to function beeswarm::beeswarm(). (Default: "none")

  • dodge.width: Numeric scalar. Width of dodge. How far apart the groups are plotted? Applies to boxes, points and bars. (Default: 0)

Line layer (paired observations, pair.by)

  • line.alpha: Numeric scalar. Transparency of lines. (Default: 0.5)

  • line.colour: Character scalar. Colour of lines. (Default: "grey70")

  • linetype: Numeric scalar. Type of lines. (Default: 1)

  • linewidth: Numeric scalar. Width of lines. (Default: 1)

Proportion bars (add.proportion = TRUE)

  • threshold: Numeric scalar. Specifies threshold for the barplots. (Default: 0)

  • bar.width: Numeric scalar. Width of proportion bars. By default, it is calculated so that the width matches with the width of boxes.

Facets

  • scales: Character scalar. Adjust scales of facets. (Default: "fixed")

  • nrow, ncol: NULL or integer scalar. Number of rows and columns of facets. (Default: NULL)

Significance (add.significance = TRUE or p.value)

  • p.value: NULL or data.frame. Pre-calculated p-values to show instead of testing with add.significance. It must have columns group1 and group2, one of p, p.adj or p.adj.signif, and the facet and x axis variables that are not compared, e.g. the output of rstatix::t_test() (see examples). (Default: NULL)

  • significance.method: Character scalar. Test used with add.significance: "wilcox.test" (or "wilcoxon") or "t.test" (or "t-test"). (Default: "wilcox.test")

  • paired: Logical scalar. Whether to use a paired test. (Default: TRUE if pair.by is specified)

  • p.adjust.method: Character scalar. Method for adjusting p-values for multiple testing, see p.adjust. (Default: "fdr")

  • mark.significance: Logical scalar. Whether to show significance levels as asterisks instead of p-values. (Default: FALSE)

  • digits: Integer scalar. Number of digits in the shown p-values. (Default: 3)

  • step.increase: Numeric scalar. Distance of significance brackets from the highest group they span, and between stacked brackets, as a fraction of the y axis range. (Default: 0.12)

  • hide.ns: Logical scalar or "p" or "p.adj". Whether to hide non-significant comparisons, as in ggpubr::stat_pvalue_manual. Hidden comparisons do not take space, so the shown brackets are stacked without gaps. (Default: FALSE)

  • Other arguments are passed to ggpubr::stat_pvalue_manual(), for example label, label.size, bracket.size, tip.length and color.

The American spellings color.by, point.color, line.color and outlier.color are also accepted.

assay.type

NULL or character scalar. Specifies the abundace table to plot. (Default: NULL)

row.var

NULL or character scalar. Specifies a variable from rowData(x) to visualize. (Default: NULL)

col.var

NULL or character scalar Specifies a variable from colData(x) to visualize. (Default: NULL)

x

NULL or character vector. Specifies a variable from colData(x) or rowData(x) to visualize in x axis. (Default: NULL)

features

NULL or character vector. If assay.type is specified, this specifies rows to visualize in different facets. If NULL, whole data is visualized as a whole. (Default: NULL)

group.by

NULL or character vector. Specifies a variable from colData(x) or rowData(x) to group observations. (Default: NULL)

Value

A ggplot2 object.

Details

A box plot is standard visualization technique to compare numeric values, such as abundance, between categorical values, such as sample groups. plotBoxplot() streamlines creation of box plots, and it offers multiple options for visualization.

See also

  • scater::plotExpression

  • scater::plotRowData

  • scater::plotColData

Examples

data("Tito2024QMP")
tse <- Tito2024QMP

tse <- transformAssay(tse, method = "relabundance")
tse <- addAlpha(tse, index = "shannon")

# Visualize alpha diversity
plotBoxplot(tse, col.var = "shannon", x = "diagnosis")


# Visualize relative abundance of top features
tse <- tse[getTop(tse, 6), ]

plotBoxplot(
    tse, assay.type = "relabundance",
    x = "diagnosis", fill.by = "diagnosis",
    features = rownames(tse), facet.by = "rownames",
    ncol = 2
)


# Add proportion bar
plotBoxplot(
    tse, assay.type = "relabundance",
    x = "diagnosis", fill.by = "diagnosis",
    features = rownames(tse), facet.by = "rownames",
    add.proportion = TRUE, threshold = 0.1
)


# Visualize only with beeswarm
plotBoxplot(
    tse, assay.type = "relabundance",
    x = "diagnosis", group.by = "diagnosis",
    colour.by = "colonoscopy",
    features = rownames(tse), facet.by = "rownames",
    point.offset = "swarm", add.box = FALSE
)
#> Warning: Removed 750 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
#> (`geom_point()`).


# Do not add points
plotBoxplot(
    tse, assay.type = "relabundance",
    fill.by = "diagnosis",
    features = rownames(tse), facet.by = "rownames",
    add.points = FALSE
)


# Calculate statistical significance with Wilcoxon test
plotBoxplot(
    tse,
    col.var = "shannon",
    fill.by = "diagnosis",
    add.significance = TRUE
)


if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Add pre-calculated p-values
# Calculate p-values
df <- meltSE(tse, add.col = TRUE)
pvals <- df |>
    rstatix::t_test(shannon ~ diagnosis) |>
    ungroup() |>
    as.data.frame()
# Add them with p.value argument
plotBoxplot(
    tse,
    x = "diagnosis",
    col.var = "shannon",
    p.value = pvals
)
} # }

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(microbiomeDataSets)

mae <- microbiomeDataSets::peerj32()
tse <- getWithColData(mae, 1)
tse[["time_point"]] <- as.character(tse[["time"]])
# Create a plot showing the change between time points in abundance of
# Akkermansia
plotBoxplot(
    tse, x = "time_point", assay.type = "counts", fill.by = "group",
    features = "Akkermansia", pair.by = "subject",
    add.change = TRUE, scales = "free"
)
} # }
